newsitem.title: USA: Mild weather aided Montana wheat seeding in week.
newsitem.headline: Mild weather aided Montana wheat seeding in week.

text.p: Seeding of winter wheat in Montana was aided by mild clear weather in the week ended on October 6, allowing crop progress to catch up with averages, the state's Agricultural Statistics Service said.

Winter wheat was 65 percent planted against 32 percent a week earlier, last year's 78 percent and the average of 69 percent. Wheat emerged was 16 percent from six a week earlier but still trailed last year's 28 pct and the 27 average pace.
"The weather has been good for seeding but many regions are looking for some additional moisture," the report said.
Topsoil moisture was rated nine percent very short, 36 percent short, 55 percent adequate and nil surplus, several percentage points drier in most categories.
The sugar beet harvest was in full swing with 25 percent of acreage harvested against eight percent a week earlier, 17 last year and 16 average.
